tickets.title: Contract completion: every v1 session field, registry entries, sample media manifest and convention-based fixture plumbing
tickets.what_to_build: The shared contracts are completed once, up front, so that no later feature ticket edits the session schema, the capability registry list or the fixture plumbing in parallel. The session schema gains every v1 field that is still missing, each optional, with a minor version bump: rally pre-roll and post-roll per session and per clip, the excluded side for audio analysis, serve and stroke key moments, serve marks (contact frame, bounce frame, bounce court position, server position, defaulted-contact flag), per-shot stroke tags, export records carrying the event-log version they were built from, a junior profile reference with the consent detail (written consent attachment, withdrawn time), a calibration stale-from time, and a bookmark note. A sample media manifest names a stable media id, file name, duration and frame rate for every sample session and practice clip; the sample library and the media renderer both read it, so neither edits the other. Fixture plumbing moves to discovery by convention: the generator imports every cases module, the validator maps fixture kind to schema by name, so adding a fixture kind means adding files and never editing a shared list. tickets.title: Scoring engine: event-log resolution, rules fold, conflicts, modes and the recalculation diff
tickets.what_to_build: The heart of the product, ported from the reference engine. Event-log resolution handles voids (undo; voiding a void is redo; voiding an event also undoes later corrections of it), supersede chains with originals kept, insertBefore for missed points, and per-set doubles orders. Structural errors carry stable codes. ScoringEngine.fold(setup, events, mode) is a pure function that always refolds from point 1. It covers every v1 format preset, Ad and No-Ad (including the deciding-point side), set and match tie-breaks, doubles rotation and receivers, lets, faults, penalties and terminations. It returns a MatchTimeline with the pre-point score, server, receiver, side, ends, changeover and pressure-point flags, provisional states after an unknown outcome, as-called versus rules-derived scores from checkpoints, the result kind and every conflict type. Rules mode and As-played mode both work. ScoringEngine.diff(before, after) lists the changed later points, game scores, set scores and the result after an edit; the stats half of the diff belongs to T05. Re-analysis may only supersede unreviewed candidates. Demo: all 74 scoring fixtures pass. The scoring conformance runner is added as its own runner file. Why blocked: T03 (the fold consumes the Swift session models and the conformance harness).
acceptance_criteria: Every jovra.fixture.scoring file (74 at time of writing) passes: deep equality with each checkpoint's expected output, including fold.changes between checkpoints.
Every E-series fixture throws a typed error whose code equals expectError.code.
Undo semantics match the fixtures: voiding a Supersede restores the previous effective value, and voiding a Void redoes it.
Re-analysis protection: a PointCandidate from a newer method version that targets a reviewed point leaves the effective view unchanged (fixture-backed).
Folding the same input twice produces byte-identical canonical output, and folding is never incremental (the public API takes the whole log).

Rules and As-played modes produce the reference outputs for the server-override fixtures; every conflict kind in the spec (serverMismatch, tiebreakAppeared, tiebreakVanished, pointsAfterMatchEnd, matchIncomplete, checkpointConflict, doublesOrderConflict, sideMismatch) is produced by at least one passing fixture.
ScoringEngine.diff on a winner flip at point 42 of the sample lists exactly the points, games, sets and result the reference fold changes, and contains no stats entries.
jovra.fixture.scoring is removed from the pending allow-list, and the jovra-core Linux CI job stays green.

tickets.title: Stats engine, JSON and CSV data export, and pooled trends
tickets.what_to_build: StatsEngine.compute(timeline, perspective) produces every stat in the rules research §6 as a Fraction carrying numerator, denominator, provenance and contributing point ids. The v1 definitions are fixed: Shots = strokeCount, rally-length buckets, second-serve points include double faults, penalty points count in total points only, tie-break games are not service games, winners exclude aces. A derived stat's provenance is the weakest of its inputs, with the count of unreviewed contributing points. Doubles adds per-server serve stats. Composition rows are rounded independently. DataExporter produces the session JSON (sidecar schema), the points and stats CSVs byte-for-byte per the CSV contracts, the Export-my-data bundle layout, and the data part of a Share Pack. TrendPool buckets sessions by range, pools numerators and denominators (never averages percentages), hides buckets below minimum samples, reports percentage-point deltas from displayed integers and excludes sample sessions. Its cases are added to the reference engine first as a new trend fixture kind. Demo: the full Jon vs Alex fixture folds, computes and exports identically to the golden files. StatsEngine.diff(beforeTimeline, afterTimeline) lists the stats a correction changes, completing the Recalculated indicator's input. The trend fixture kind is added as new files only (cases module, schema, runner file). Why blocked: T04 (stats are computed over the MatchTimeline).

tickets.title: Session store: single-writer document store, state facets, index, trash, migration and MediaLibrary custody
tickets.what_to_build: The local-first document store of ADR-0002, as package code with no app files. Each session is a folder with media and one versioned session document written atomically as canonical JSON. SessionStore is a single-writer actor: create, load, append([Event]) as one atomic write for a batch, update(facet:), updateRecording(_:) for capture metadata, list with search over players, courts and notes and filters for type, state and sample, trash, restore from trash, purge (requires a confirmation token), rebuild the index, migrate older documents forward and quarantine an unreadable document with a reason. The four facets (original, analysis, review, archive) are independent enums. Head-to-head and opponent history are queries. MediaLibrary in JovraMedia takes custody of session media, reports per-session sizes and derived-cache sizes, and exposes the include-originals-in-device-backup API; originals are excluded from iCloud device backup by default (D7). The UI row for that setting belongs to T51. After this ticket no later ticket edits the store; a missing API goes into a small store-fix PR. Why blocked: T03 (stores the Swift session models as canonical JSON).

tickets.title: Capture engine: segment pipeline, write-ahead journal, fixture camera and device budget
tickets.what_to_build: Recording that never loses a session (ADR-0010, D9), as package code. CaptureEngine composes a CaptureSource with one segment pipeline: an AVAssetWriter writing fragmented MP4 segments (about 2 s fragments) behind a write-ahead CaptureJournal that records segments, gaps with reasons, the saved-through heartbeat, and thermal and frame-rate changes. CameraSource is used on device: ultra-wide when the court needs it, locked frame rate, stabilization off, focus, exposure and white balance locked after framing. FixtureCamera is used on the simulator and streams the fixture-camera clip with audio, with test hooks for interruptions, thermal rungs, low storage, crashes and media-services resets, and an injected clock so tests do not run in wall time. DeviceBudget reads free space, battery, Low Power Mode and thermal state behind a protocol with a fake.
